The test image shows a mature soybean stem with **dense black specks (pycnidia) scattered across the stem surface**, combined with dried/mature pods. This is the hallmark sign of Diaporthe pod and stem blight — "linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature soybean stems." The reference images confirm this pattern with the characteristic black fungal structures on stems. There's also some whitish material visible but the dominant diagnostic feature is clearly the pycnidia on the stem.
